paragraphs: It was Saturday morning, and Lily was awake. She looked out of the window. The sky was gray, and the rain fell on the roof. It was a cold, windy day. "Oh no!" said Lily. "It isn't sunny, so we can't play pirates in the park." Mia ran in from the house next door. She wore a yellow coat and blue boots. Her hair was wet. "I have my pirate hat, but we don't have any sun," said Mia. Tom came in and smiled. "Why not play pirates inside?" he asked.

The children made a ship in the living room. Two chairs were the ship, and a blue blanket was the sea. Mom's green plants stood by the window, so the room was a jungle. "Most pirates have a map," said Mia. Lily drew one with a red pencil. Pip sat on the blanket in a paper hat. He looked like a very small pirate dog. "Where is the treasure?" asked Tom. "Under the table!" shouted Lily. They could not go out, but they had fun. Then Pip took the map and ran. "Stop, Pip!" laughed Mia.

At twelve o'clock, the rain stopped. The sun came out. "It's sunny and hot now," said Mom. "Wear your hats!" The children put on their hats and went to the garden. The grass was wet. Pip jumped in the water and ran in a circle. He had the map in his mouth, and it was very wet. "Is that our treasure map?" asked Tom. Mom brought a plate of fruit. "Here is your treasure!" she said. Pirates like every kind of weather.
